name: Amlodipine
route_note: oral tablet or suspension once daily; many fixed-dose combinations
owner: generic (many); Norvasc brand held by Viatris

discovery.note: Designed as a long-acting dihydropyridine with gradual onset. Year of first patent (1982), per Wikipedia.

tagline: Long-acting once-daily calcium channel blocker, a global hypertension mainstay
summary: Amlodipine is a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes arterial smooth muscle. It is one of the most prescribed drugs worldwide for hypertension and chronic stable or vasospastic angina, and appears in many combination pills.
mechanism: Amlodipine binds L-type voltage-gated calcium channels (Cav1.2) in vascular smooth muscle, reducing calcium entry and causing arterial vasodilation and lower peripheral resistance.
At therapeutic doses it has little effect on cardiac conduction or contractility. Its very long half-life gives smooth, gradual blood pressure control with little reflex tachycardia.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Norvasc.

history.title: ALLHAT
history.detail: Amlodipine is as effective as chlorthalidone for coronary outcomes in hypertension, with more heart failure.

history.title: ASCOT-BPLA
history.detail: An amlodipine-based regimen reduces total mortality and stroke versus an atenolol-based regimen.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic amlodipine becomes available in the US.

history.title: ACCOMPLISH
history.detail: Benazepril plus amlodipine outperforms benazepril plus hydrochlorothiazide.

serious: Worsening angina or MI on initiation (rare)

facts: Ankle oedema is dose-related and caused by precapillary vasodilation, not fluid retention, so diuretics help little.
It is one of the most prescribed medicines in the United States.
